title: KV quantization ablation: INT8 vs FP8 latency and quality profiling
creator: Maya Rodriguez
description: Run controlled KV-cache quantization experiments to compare INT8 and FP8 encodings for cached keys/values. Goals: 1) quantify token-level latency improvements from storing KV in lower precision, 2) measure end-to-end quality impact across representative workloads (chat, code, long-context reasoning), 3) validate calibration workflows that produce per-layer scaling factors safe for production rollouts, and 4) produce a rollout policy (canary thresholds, fallback) and patch PR for runtime and model packaging. Deliverables: experiment matrix, calibrated profiles for selected models, evaluation report with latency/quality trade-off curves, suggested runtime changes and safety checks for automatic fallback.

experiment_notes: Calibration corpus: 2000 prompts (50% dialog/instruction, 30% code, 20% long-context summaries).
Calibration methods tested: per-tensor minmax, per-channel symmetric, per-channel KL tuning (10 iterations), percentile clipping at 99.9th.

Quantization targets: KV projection outputs (K,V), attention softmax intermediate caches; model weights kept at FP16 for these experiments except a small sweep for mixed-weight INT8 on linear projections.
Observed failure mode: sustained KV reuse across >512 tokens amplifies small scale mismatches leading to token divergence in multi-step reasoning chains.

Latency tradeoffs: FP16 baseline 14.2ms/token, INT8-KV ~11.3ms (-20%), FP8-KV ~10.6ms (-25%). Token throughput improves consistently, but tail latency variance increases slightly with INT8 due to dequantize hotspots.
Quality tradeoffs: average log-prob delta relative to FP16: INT8 -0.18 nats, FP8 -0.09 nats. Downstream metric deltas within acceptance for most customers except strict-recall reasoning workloads.
Cost impact: projected 30% reduction in GPU memory pressure for serving which allows 20% higher batch packing and ~12% unit-cost savings for high-concurrency customers when KV quantized.
Recommended safe profile (prod candidate): FP8-KV with KL-calibrated scales for values + symmetric per-channel for keys; reject if eval delta exceeds thresholds in the calibration gate.
Rollout policy: canary 5% traffic -> monitor top-1 token delta, MATH EM, latency p95. Auto-fallback to FP16 if top-1 delta > 1% or MATH EM delta > 1.5% over 30-minute window.
Open questions: Should we expose 'kv_quant_profile' in model metadata to allow per-customer policy? How to attribute failures to quantized KV vs. other model changes in multi-variable rollouts?
